claims: Palencia is the capital of Palencia province in Castilla y León.
Palencia is in north-central Spain.
Palencia Cathedral is known as San Antolín.
Palencia Cathedral is known as "the unknown beauty".
Palencia Cathedral is one of Spain's largest cathedrals.
Palencia Cathedral features a mix of Visigoth, Romanesque, and Gothic styles.
Cristo del Otero is a 21-meter-high post-cubist statue of Christ.
Victorio Macho sculpted Cristo del Otero.
Cristo del Otero offers panoramic views of Palencia.
Calle Mayor is the main commercial artery in Palencia.
Calle Mayor is characterized by its long arcaded street.
Plaza Mayor is a Neoclassical square in Palencia.
Plaza Mayor is home to the Town Hall.
Church of San Miguel has a Romanesque tower.
Legend says Cid Campeador was married at Church of San Miguel.
Museo de Palencia houses archaeological artifacts from the Roman, Visigoth, and Medieval periods.
Palencia was originally inhabited by the Vaccaei people.
Palencia was occupied by Romans as Pallantia.
Palencia was occupied by Visigoths.
In 1208, Alfonso VIII established the first university in Spain in Palencia.
The Canal of Castile is near Palencia.
The Canal of Castile is 18th-century.
The Canal of Castile was designed for shipping grain.
Palencia is situated in the Tierra de Campos region.
Palencia is along the Carrión River.
Palencia is in the autonomous community of Castile and León.
Palencia is connected via high-speed AVE train to Madrid.
Palencia is connected via high-speed AVE train to León.
Palencia is noted as one of the cities with the most green space per inhabitant in Spain.
Palencia province has one of Europe’s highest concentrations of Romanesque art.
Frómista has Romanesque art.
Aguilar de Campoo has Romanesque art.
Fuentes Carrionas is a nature reserve near Palencia.
Canal de Castilla is near Palencia
